todo_line: - [ ] 001 Implement the actor-bearing custom-group removal use case through the 063 Club-owned authorization boundary, validating custom-group and actor/target club identities, permitting self/last-member removal, and emitting the existing `GroupMemberRemoved` without changing club membership or roles.
outcome: Provide one public, actor-authenticated custom-group removal write path that is authorized from current Club aggregate state, allows member/admin and self/last-member cases, and records only the existing GroupMemberRemoved fact while preserving club membership and roles.
scope: Add a distinct actor-bearing custom-group removal command carrying club_id, group_id, target membership_id/person_id, and actor_person_id; keep the existing actor-free RemoveGroupMember command internal and unchanged.
Expose Memba.Membership.remove_custom_group_member/1 and /2 as a thin command-construction/dispatch boundary, and register the new command on the existing Club route in Membership.Router/App.
In Memba.Membership.Club, validate the loaded club identity and typed group, target membership/person, and actor person identities; reject unknown/system groups.
Authorize from current Club aggregate state using the 063 rule: the active actor is either an active member of that custom group or has active club.manage_members permission.

Validate that the target membership/person pair is an active membership of the same club and an active member of the selected custom group for a new transition; preserve safe exact-retry behavior without allowing an unauthorized actor to probe or mutate membership.
Permit removing another member, removing oneself, an outside club admin removing a member without joining, and removal of the last group member.
Reuse GroupMemberRemoved and existing aggregate apply/projector behavior. Do not emit ClubMemberRemoved or club-role events and do not archive/delete/change the group.
Add focused command-shape, router/app registration, aggregate authorization/identity/invariant, public API, dispatch/event, and projection tests.
scope_exclusions: Do not change ClearRemovedGroupMemberFollows, Messaging follow commands/APIs, cleanup ordering/generation behavior, or claim TODO 004-008.
Do not change conversation/read/action authorization, queued delivery handoff, or LiveView refresh behavior from TODO 009-011.
Do not add Leave/Remove UI, confirmations, post-removal screens, component/design changes, or empty-state UI from TODO 012-014.
Do not edit acceptance feature files, browser step definitions, iteration plan/ADRs/reference docs, or runner-debt tags; TODO 015-016 remain pending.
Do not run or claim the final exact-state dev check obligation in TODO 017 as completed by this packet.

constraints: Treat plan.md as authoritative and do not edit it.
Use the Club aggregate's current event-sourced state for authorization and identity decisions; do not authorize this command with projection preflight reads.
Preserve trusted raw AddGroupMember/RemoveGroupMember behavior for system-group policy, backfill, and fixture callers.
Keep GroupMemberRemoved actor-free and JSON-compatible; actor identity belongs on the command/use-case boundary, not the historical fact.
A custom-group removal must not alter active club membership, Admin/other roles, group identity, email address, history, or lifecycle status.
Everyone and Admin must remain inaccessible through the custom-group API, including forged direct dispatch.
Do not introduce a last-member floor. Applying the last removal leaves the group definition intact.
Pin removal idempotency explicitly. In particular, do not weaken current actor authorization merely to make a former ordinary member's self-removal retry return success.
Follow the repository Elixir/test guidance: one module per file, focused tests, no sleeps, and no new dependency.
focused_validation: From web/, run the new custom-group removal dispatch test together with test/memba/membership/club_test.exs, test/memba/membership/group_command_event_modules_test.exs, test/memba/membership/app_test.exs, and test/memba/membership/public_api_test.exs.
Prove the public command dispatches to aggregate_uuid == club_id and a successful new removal contains exactly the existing GroupMemberRemoved identity tuple.
Prove current member, outside-admin, unauthorized outsider/inactive actor, target mismatch/inactive/cross-club, malformed identity, and Everyone/Admin cases.
Prove self-removal and last-member removal, then inspect aggregate/projected state to show the group remains and the target's active club membership and roles are unchanged.
Prove an exact repeat does not append a second GroupMemberRemoved while retaining the selected authorization semantics.
completion_evidence_required: List every changed file and identify the new public function, actor-bearing command, router registration, and Club execute path.
Report the exact focused test command and pass/fail totals; do not report unavailable or setup-failed tests as passing.
Report the observed command result/event list for a new removal and for the idempotent repeat.
Report evidence that self/last-member removal succeeds while club membership, Admin role/permission, group definition, and trusted raw RemoveGroupMember behavior remain intact.
Confirm no excluded follow-cleanup, Messaging, delivery, LiveView/UI, acceptance-feature, ADR/reference, or plan work was changed.
Identify any unaccepted candidate changes by their originating commit/diff if work is returned incomplete or requires replan.
